newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: UBS sees little change in provisions in 96.
newsitem.headline: UBS sees little change in provisions in 96.

text.p: Union Bank of Switzerland (UBS) chief executive Mathis Cabiallavetta said he expected the bank's value adjustments, provisions and losses to total around 1.2 billion Swiss francs in 1996.
Value adjustments, provisions and losses totalled 1.17 billion in 1995. They amounted to 804 million francs in the first six months of 1996.
"It could be around 1.2 billion (Swiss francs), Cabiallavetta said at a news conference, adding, "If we were below 1.2 billion francs I would be quite happy."
Cabiallavetta also said in response to a question that a return on equity of nine percent for UBS in 1996 was possible.
